hypothesis: Wingless F1B's 144 original/counterfactual false positives are caused by low-separation learned link-gating probabilities, not near-alias substitution; stronger already-existing CODED equality gate improves accuracy and specificity.
controls: Evaluate exactly four prefixed arms: original F1B frozen trained gate, preexisting W-F1 fixed sharp control (13,0,-6.5), independently specified near-binary coded gate (20,0,-15), and zero-link negative control (0,0,-30); no training/refit/tuning. Original F1/F1B are NOT rerun. Same 576-byte resident memory and 4-hop coded decoder.
cohort: NEW DEV ONLY 24 seeds [39600,39624), graph families 4-7, four cuts, 384 graph states, two questions each, 384 positives and 384 negatives; independent of F1B seeds 39312-39335. New adversarial aliases from frozen F1B procedure. Not sealed first use.
rubric: CODED_GATE_SHARPNESS_EXPLAINS_FROZEN_FALSE_POSITIVES iff preexisting fixed sharp gate stress accuracy >=0.95, stress false-positive rate <=0.05, stress accuracy exceeds frozen trained gate by >=0.10, and frozen-gate false positive rate exceeds fixed by >=0.20. Otherwise GATE_SHARPNESS_CAUSAL_DIAGNOSTIC_UNRESOLVED.
limits: Even a positive result supports CODED equality gate sharpness, not learned entity identity, transferable cognition, native NCI01, AGI or RSI. Study is developmental only and cannot revise F1/F1B prereg verdicts.
authority: No sealed cohort, accepted-ref mutation, queue/dispatch/controller/workflow ownership, FORGE R32/R33, KTRADE, broker or production; GitHub workflow uses one bounded source-pinned development evaluation with final full Go regression.
